Although countless times, waking and sleeping, St. George had humoured himself in the outworn pastime of dreaming what he would do if he were to inherit a million dollars, his imagination had never marveled its way to the situation's less poignant advantages.

67988-the-vortex-a-play-in-three-acts.title: A Play in Three Acts
67988-the-vortex-a-play-in-three-acts.creator: Noel Coward
67988-the-vortex-a-play-in-three-acts.description: A book by Noel Coward. PAWNIE [_Wandering round the room_] Not at all, but I do like things to be good and right. HELEN Well, I don’t consider the new frieze in your bathroom either good or right. PAWNIE How can you, Helen! It’s too marvelous for words. Parelli designed it specially for me. arxiv-2201-06817.title: Buildup of the Magnetic Flux Ropes in Homologous Solar Eruptions
arxiv-2201-06817.creator: Rui Wang, Ying D. Liu, Shangbin Yang, Huidong Hu
arxiv-2201-06817.description: Abstract Homologous coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are an interesting phenomenon, and it is possible to investigate the formation of CMEs by comparing multi-CMEs under a homologous physical condition. AR 11283 had been present on the solar surface for several days when a bipole emerged on 2011 September 4.

arxiv-2303-00117.title: Study of the Inflationary Spectrum in the Presence of Quantum Gravity Corrections
arxiv-2303-00117.creator: Giulia Maniccia * \orcidG, Giovanni Montani, Leonardo Torcellini
arxiv-2303-00117.description: Abstract After a brief review of the different approaches to predicting the possible quantum gravity corrections to quantum field theory, we discuss in some detail the formulation based on a Gaussian reference frame fixing. Then, we utilize this scenario in the determination of the inflationary spectrum of primordial perturbations.

arxiv-2310-14840.title: Transparency at the Source: Evaluating and Interpreting Language Models With Access to the True Distribution
arxiv-2310-14840.creator: Jaap Jumelet Willem Zuidema
arxiv-2310-14840.description: Abstract We present a setup for training, evaluating and interpreting neural language models, that uses artificial, language-like data. The data is generated using a massive probabilistic grammar (based on state-split PCFGs), that is itself derived from a large natural language corpus, but also provides us complete control over the generative process.

arxiv-2412-18889.title: Experimental particle production in time-dependent spacetimes: a one-dimensional scattering problem
arxiv-2412-18889.creator: Marius Sparn, 1∗ Elinor Kath, 1 Nikolas Liebster, 1 Jelte Duchene, 1 Christian F. Schmidt, 2 Mireia Tolosa-Simeón, 3 Álvaro Parra-López, 4 Stefan Floerchinger, 2 Helmut Strobel 1 and Markus K. Oberthaler 1 1 Kirchhoff-Institut für Physik, Universität Heidelberg, Im Neuenheimer Feld 227, 69120 Heidel
arxiv-2412-18889.description: Abstract We experimentally study cosmological particle production in a two-dimensional Bose-Einstein condensate, whose density excitations map to an analog cosmology. The expansion of spacetime is realized with tunable interactions. The particle spectrum can be understood through an analogy to quantum mechanical scattering, in which the dynamics of the spacetime metric determine the shape of the scattering potential.

arxiv-2505-16662.title: Joint Magnetometer-IMU Calibration via Maximum A Posteriori Estimation
arxiv-2505-16662.creator: Chuan Huang, Gustaf Hendeby, Isaac Skog
arxiv-2505-16662.description: Abstract This paper presents a new method for jointly calibrating a magnetometer and inertial measurement unit (IMU), focusing on balancing calibration accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed method is based on a maximum a posteriori estimation framework, treating both the calibration parameters and orientation trajectory of the sensors as unknowns.

arxiv-2506-12654.title: Robust and efficient multiple-unit switchback experimentation
arxiv-2506-12654.creator: Paul Missault Lorenzo Masoero Christian Delbé Thomas Richardson Guido Imbens
arxiv-2506-12654.description: Abstract User-randomized A/B testing has emerged as the gold standard for online experimentation. However, when this kind of approach is not feasible due to legal, ethical or practical considerations, experimenters have to consider alternatives like item-randomization. Item-randomization is often met with skepticism due to its poor empirical performance.

arxiv-2506-23715.title: Towards a Science of Developer eXperience (DevX) Publication type: column
arxiv-2506-23715.creator: Benoit Combemale
arxiv-2506-23715.description: Abstract As software continues to permeate nearly every facet of modern life, the complexity and ubiquity of digital services underscore the need for sustainable, effective, and inclusive software development practices. Although software engineering has made significant progress in technical challenges since its inception, the human experience of those involved in software creation, broadly defined as developers, remains underexplored.

arxiv-2509-24689.title: 𝒦 ​ ℒ \mathcal{K}\mathcal{L} and Lyapunov Approaches for Discrete-time Peak Computation Problems
arxiv-2509-24689.creator: Assalé Adjé
arxiv-2509-24689.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a method to solve discrete-time peak computation problems (DPCPs for short). DPCPs are optimization problems that consist of maximizing a function over the reachable values set of a discrete-time dynamical system. The optimal value of a DPCP can be rewritten as the supremum of the sequence of optimal values.

pmc-11522843.title: Fatiguing exercise reduces cellular passive Young's modulus in human vastus lateralis muscle
pmc-11522843.creator: Grace E. Privett, Austin W. Ricci, Larry L. David, Karen Wiedenfeld Needham, Yong How Tan, Karina H. Nakayama, Damien M. Callahan
pmc-11522843.description: Previous studies demonstrated that acute fatiguing exercise transiently reduces whole‐muscle stiffness, which might contribute to increased risk of injury and impaired contractile performance. We sought to elucidate potential intracellular mechanisms underlying these reductions. To that end, the cellular passive Young's modulus was measured in muscle fibres from healthy, young males and females.

pmc-11525969.title: Accurate molecular recognition from the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital
pmc-11525969.creator: Xuehua Zhou, Shixing Yang, Chao Han
pmc-11525969.description: The quantification of the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital level (LUMO) for molecular semiconductors is of great importance, because it determines the charge transport process and hence the performances of diverse electronic devices. Unfortunately, there is always lack of a convenient technique to determine the intrinsic LUMO.

pmc-11678153.title: The Growing Phenomenon of ‘Frozen’ Virus Genome Sequences and Their Likely Origin in Research Facility Escapes
pmc-11678153.creator: Steven E Massey, Paolo Calistri
pmc-11678153.description: ‘Frozen’ virus genome sequences are sampled from outbreaks and have unusually low sequence divergence when compared to genome sequences from historical strains. A growing number of ‘frozen’ virus genome sequences are being reported as virus genome sequencing becomes more common.

pmc-12704688.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Piperacillin-Tazobactam or Fluoroquinolones Versus Third-Generation Cephalosporins in Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-12704688.creator: Jie Siang See, Sin Yee Wong
pmc-12704688.description: Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP) remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality among patients with cirrhosis. Third-generation cephalosporins (TGCs) have long been considered standard empiric therapy in major guidelines such as the British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG), the European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL), and the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD).

pmc-12764044.title: The role of external factors in shaping the supply and demand of general practitioners in Iran: a qualitative study
pmc-12764044.creator: Mohammadreza Amiresmaili, Mohammad Hossein Mehrolhassani, Mahla Iranmanesh
pmc-12764044.description: General practitioners are crucial for community health, but their numbers and distribution in Iran face challenges due to factors outside the healthcare system. In Iran—as in many health systems experiencing epidemiologic transition, fiscal constraints, and specialist-oriented care—primary care capacity is a key determinant of equity, access, and cost containment.

pmc-13382092.title: Gene transcriptional expression of cerebral blood flow alterations in Parkinson's disease: a transcription-neuroimaging association study
pmc-13382092.creator: Jiaqi Cui, Qiane Yu, Haifeng Ran, Kexin Huang, Jie Hu, Tijiang Zhang
pmc-13382092.description: AimDespite the intimate link between cerebral blood flow (CBF) alterations and Parkinson's disease (PD) pathogenesis and cognitive decline, the precise pathophysiological mechanisms driving this relationship remain elusive. This study seeks to correlate changes in CBF with regional gene expression to advance mechanistic understanding of the disease.

pmc-13582252.title: H5N1 clade 2.3.2.1e lineage transition in Lao PDR during 2023–2024 associated with regional spread and human infection risk-associated receptor-binding features
pmc-13582252.creator: Duc Duong Than, Boyoon Chang, Eun Lee, Watthana Theppangna, Seon-Ju Yeo, Hyun Park
pmc-13582252.description: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 viruses clade 2.3.2.1e has re-emerged in the Indochinese Peninsula, raising concerns about regional spread and zoonotic risk. We characterized eight H5N1 viruses isolated from 32 environmental and poultry-derived samples collected in Lao People’s Democratic Republic (Lao PDR) live bird markets during 2023–2024. Whole-genome and phylogenetic analyses showed that all isolates belonged to clade 2.3.2.
